name: i-have-adhd
description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
one_liner: A tweak for your AI coding assistant that makes it give you the next action first instead of burying it inside a long explanation.
buyer: Honestly a niche personal-productivity tweak for individual developers who find AI assistants too verbose, not something with a distinct paying business buyer.
business_use_cases: An individual developer installs it personally to cut down time spent scrolling past preamble to find the actual command to run.
A dev tools educator references it as a teaching example of prompt-engineering for concise agent output.
A productivity coach working with ADHD developers mentions it as a free tool alongside other workflow advice.

money_ideas.idea: There's no real direct revenue model: it's a free, personal workflow tweak, not something a buyer would pay for on its own.

steal_this: There's no real weekend business in the tool itself, but a productivity coach could write a short paid guide on configuring AI tools for ADHD-friendly workflows, using this as one example.
